chunks: Ali ibn al-Sindi from Hammad from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whatever the Muhrim fears for himself from beasts, snakes, and others, let him kill it; and if they do not seek you out, do not seek them out."

key_terms.اَلسِّبَاعِ: Beasts of prey or wild animals
key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.فَلْيَقْتُلْهُ: Let him kill it (legal permissive ruling)

ai.seo_question: What animals can a person in Ihram kill if they threaten their safety?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *al-istithna'* (exemption) within the strict prohibitions of Ihram, prioritizing self-preservation (*nafs*) over ritual purity when facing genuine danger from wild beasts or snakes. It establishes a legal nuance where the Muhrim is not required to wait for an attack but may act preemptively against threats, while maintaining the general rule of non-aggression towards non-threatening creatures. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between necessary defense and prohibited hunting during the sacred state.
